subject: Post-call: Warmup timing, queueing behavior & SLO matrix
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Simon Kwan <simon.k@brightmart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Warmup timing, queueing behavior & SLO matrix

Hi Simon — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical run: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~1.2k concurrent active users, periodic spikes up to ~5k concurrent for 60–180s during promotional windows.
- Query mix: 65% short, completion-style prompts (~<256 tokens), 35% streaming chat where client receives tokens as they’re generated.
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency goal for short queries ~250ms; streaming clients expect token emission >= 200 tokens/sec for long responses.
- Availability tolerance: customer expects <0.5% request failure during normal ops, and graceful degradation (stream fallback to chunked responses) during bursts.

Open technical checkpoints (what we need to confirm)
1) Warm pool sizing: you asked for guidance on how many prewarmed instances to keep. We should define warm pool as instances with model loaded, KV warmed, and ready to stream (no cold init).
2) Scale-up time: you reported that past stacks saw 40–60s cold-starts; we need to align on acceptable scale-up windows and whether a short buffer queue is allowed.
3) Queueing policy: define max queue wait, drop vs. fail behavior, and options for request prioritization.
4) Measurement & SLO: confirm whether p95 will be measured from request arrival to final token emitted (end-to-end) or inference-only.

Proposed next steps
- Redwood to provide an initial SLA matrix and warmup checklist (attached).
- Technical deep-dive / runbook review with your infra ops and our performance team: propose Tuesday, Mar 8 for a staged load test (duration 2 hours).
- We'll draft a mutual action plan and share a HubSpot deal link for sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-warmup-checklist.xlsx, sla-matrix-v2.pdf
Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-warmup-map

Are you comfortable with the proposed scope for the Mar 8 session? If so, we'll loop in engineering and confirm time slots.

Thanks,
Lauren

- The p95 goal is intended as end-to-end (client -> response complete). We’ll expect network overhead included.
- For streaming: the 200 tokens/sec is a soft target — we'd like to see consistent chunked emissions during peaks (no long pauses >500ms between chunks).

Folks — forwarding Simon's quick confirmation. Please see the questions above; I captured our asks below and we need short tactical answers so we can confirm Mar 8 load test and a small M.A.P. for BrightMart. These are internal only — do not send until we agree.

Action items / technical clarifications needed from infra/runtime team:
A) Measurement: define how Redwood reports p95 — is our telemetry end-to-end by default, or do we provide both inference-only and end-to-end metrics? Need exact metric names.
B) Warm pool definition: clarify resource definition (GPU model, memory footprint, and whether warm = KV warmed + tokenizer cached). Also provide estimated memory and GPU utilization per instance for BrightMart's 35% streaming profile.
C) Cold-start window: give a 95th percentile cold-start time for currently supported models (e.g., base-7B fp16 vs quantized 7B). We should give a range and note dependence on model size and platform (A100 vs H100).
D) Queueing policy: what is our default max wait (s), are we using sliding-window queueing, and do we offer graceful degradation (stream chunking/fallback) vs hard fail?
E) Priming behavior: does our warm cache include prefix KV priming per customer? If not, what are options for prepriming?

I attached a warmup checklist and SLA matrix for reference — please update the checklist with realistic numbers and return by EOD tomorrow so I can send to Simon. If you prefer, we can do a 30-min sync tomorrow at 11:00 to align.

Thanks,
Lauren

Hi Lauren / Simon — answering the internal checklist items and proposing a test configuration. Summaries first, details below.

Quick answers
- Measurement: we expose both inference-only and end-to-end p95; by default the SLA document references end-to-end (request ingress -> last packet). Metric names: redwood.latency.p95.e2e and redwood.latency.p95.inference.
- Warm pool: defined as instances with model binaries loaded, KV cache initialized to recent traffic patterns, and worker process ready to accept requests. For BrightMart's profile we recommend a warm pool of 40 GPU instances (A100 40GB) to cover a sustained 1.2k concurrent baseline with headroom for short spikes.
- Cold-start 95th percentile: 38–55s for 7B-class models (fp16) on A100; quantized models can be as low as 12–20s depending on quant libs.
- Queueing policy: default is sliding-window queue with 60s max wait, then fail with explicit 503 + retryable flag. We also support a prioritized queue where premium traffic is allowed to skip a soft queue for up to N instances.
- Streaming: token emission is measured at the runtime level; we guarantee emission pacing and provide backpressure hooks. For BrightMart target of 200 tokens/sec we recommend using an adaptive warm pool and an initial priming call to populate KV for common prompts.

Proposed staging test on Mar 8 (2-hour window)
- Phase 1 (30m): baseline steady 1.2k concurrency, validate p50/p95/p99 (e2e and inference).
- Phase 2 (40m): ramp spikes to 5k concurrency for 2x periods of 90s, validate queueing behavior and streaming chunk consistency.
- Phase 3 (40m): failover scenarios — simulate region fallback and model variant downgrade to quantify graceful degradation.

Attachments & docs
- sla-matrix-v2.pdf (attached) — I updated the cold-start ranges and queue defaults.
- redwood-warmup-checklist.xlsx (attached) — filled recommended warm pool counts and priming steps.
- Test plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-warmup-map

Simon — if that aligns, we'll send an invite for Mar 8 10:30 PT + include Monica and our runtime lead. Also please share an ops contact for traffic generation and any authentication constraints (IP allowlist, cert pinning).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
